data.narrative:
Cylib is a Series A climate & energy company that has raised €140M+ in total capital, comprising a €55M equity round alongside €26.1M in NRW grants and €63.4M in BMWE grants. The broader Climate & Energy sector contains nine peer companies, with one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

A peer-median valuation approach proves inapplicable here due to insufficient depth within filtered peer cohorts. Of the nine same-sector peers identified, none satisfied the narrowing criteria of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier filters simultaneously—a minimum of three datapoints is required for reliable triangulation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias and obscure sector-specific risk and growth dynamics. With only one public comparable available and eight private peers spread across different funding stages and business models, traditional multiples-based approaches lack the precision necessary for a defensible valuation range.

The primary uncertainty constraining valuation analysis is the absence of a sufficiently dense and homogeneous peer set at Series A within climate & energy infrastructure. A narrower comp universe—particularly additional same-stage private or public peers with comparable business models—would enable revenue multiple, EBITDA multiple, or DCF-anchored triangulation. Until such datapoints emerge or Cylib's operating metrics become visible, quantitative valuation synthesis remains premature. The substantial grant funding (€89.5M of €140M+) should be separately considered as it reflects de-risking by public entities rather than pure market-based pricing signals.
